headline: A 2022 law sets up federal research, education, and awareness efforts on valvular heart disease, including a workshop on mitral valve prolapse.
what_it_does: The law lets the National Institutes of Health research valvular heart disease, which is damage to or disease of the valves that control blood flow in the heart, working with the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. It requires that institute to hold a workshop on mitral valve prolapse, a condition where a heart valve does not seal properly. It also directs the Department of Health and Human Services to develop best practices for treating valvular heart disease and allows it to run education and awareness projects.

who_it_affects.group: People with valvular heart disease or mitral valve prolapse
who_it_affects.how: Federal research and awareness efforts may lead to better information and treatment guidance for their condition over time.

who_it_affects.group: Families and caregivers of people with heart valve conditions
who_it_affects.how: Expanded public education and awareness projects may give them more information about these diseases.

who_it_affects.group: Health care providers who treat heart valve disease
who_it_affects.how: HHS best practices may give them federal guidance on treatment approaches.

who_it_affects.group: Medical researchers at NIH and NHLBI
who_it_affects.how: The law gives them authority to conduct or support research on valvular heart disease.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted December 20, 2022; the summary does not list any other specific effective dates or deadlines.
